title: Corroded metal: rust and verdigris
purpose: Generate tileable PBR maps of corroding metal: rust on steel or verdigris on copper, with layered oxide, pits, flaking crust and drip stains, and a metallic map that separates bare metal from oxide. Use for industrial props, ships, pipes and old roofs.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python metal_corrosion.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: coverage
parameters.meaning: Share of the surface under oxide.

parameters.name: patch_scale
parameters.meaning: Noise cells across the tile for the corrosion patches: higher values give smaller patches.

parameters.name: pitting
parameters.meaning: Density and depth of pits in the oxide.

parameters.name: streaks
parameters.meaning: Strength of the oxide stains running down from each patch.

parameters.name: flaking
parameters.meaning: Raised, cracked crust in the thick middle of the patches.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Steel plate with orange-brown rust patches and light drip stains.

presets.name: heavy_rust
presets.description: Steel almost covered in thick flaking rust with deep pits.

presets.name: verdigris
presets.description: Copper with blue-green patina and brown oxide rims.

presets.name: light_bloom
presets.description: Mostly bare polished steel with small early rust spots.

limits: Corrosion is a noise-driven pattern, not an electrochemical simulation; it ignores edges, welds and drainage of a real object. Drip stains always run toward the bottom of the tile. Metal colours are artistic approximations of reflectance. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate.
technique_references: Thresholded fractional Brownian motion as a growth mask
Per-octave lattice offsets to avoid gradient-noise lattice zeros
Downward exponential trail per column, swept twice for wrap-around
Worley noise for pits and crust cracks
glTF metallic-roughness split between metal and oxide
